newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares in waiting for reweighting of index.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares in waiting for reweighting of index.

text.p: Belgium's leading shares were trapped in narrow ranges on Monday as the market began a long vigil ahead of Friday's reweighting of the Bel-20 index.
Volume in the 20 blue chips underlying the index was a thin 1.2 billion Belgian francs. Dealers said they did not expect more action unless U.S. financial markets experienced a sudden correction.
"If you were a fund manager...would you buy now and hope there's no correction or would you wait?," one trader commented.
Even a firm bond market had little impact on prices, dealers said. "Everyone's waiting for Friday," another dealer said.
Energy group Electrabel, which traditionally moves in tandem with bond prices, rose a meagre 20 francs, although one dealer said one brokerage had been a steady seller of the share.

Bank Kredietbank, which will see its weight in the Bel-20 index doubled from Friday, rose 125 francs to 10,350 francs. Dealers said the share was helped by first half results released last week as much as the Bel-20 effect.
With price movements among the main issues limited, most of Monday's biggest changes were in smaller stocks on the back of or ahead of earnings news.
Holiday parks operator Walibi, which warned on Friday it would slide to a current loss in 1996, fell 5.9 percent to 1,364 Belgian francs - an all time low.

Fast food group Quick fell 15 to 2,565 francs. After the close, Quick, confirming earlier warnings, reported profit in the six months to June 30 fell to seven from 147 million francs due to Europe's beef crisis. Full year earnings would be 30 to 35 percent down on 1995, the company said.

But photos group Spector, which announced a big acquisition recently, ended up 15 at 2,160 francs ahead of news that first half pre-tax profit slipped to 49 million francs. -- Nick Antonovics, Brussels newsroom, tel. +322 287 6810
